steps.content: [Beach, Sunset]

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Huff... Huff...
You finally shake off the last of the underwater horrors and drag your soaked, exhausted bodies onto the shore, collapsing onto the coarse sand.
A crackling campfire slowly steams the water from your coats, its warmth a welcome anchor to reality.
The sun bleeds slowly toward the horizon, calming the sea. The air hangs heavy with the scent of salt, the silence broken only by the crackle of the fire and the ragged sound of your own breathing.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Sun's actually out. Shame it's almost gone.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: See those clouds? Moving fast. Not a good sign. Tonight's storm will be worse.
You've faced every storm alone so far. This time there are two of us. We'll be fine. We worked like a good team just now.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: That look... it's really the same.
She lies on her side beside you, a low curse escaping under her breath, one she didn't intend for you to hear.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Herbert, in the cellar... Miles, heading back from the sea... They had the same look you did just now.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Reckless. But so damn bright.
She closes her eyes, her attention turning to the gentle rhythm of the waves and the soft crackle of the fire.
You turn your head to look at your hard-won prize. The generator rests beside you, its metal casing glinting in the sunset's afterglow.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Tide comes in after sunset. Fix the lighthouse now, or don't bother.
I know. But there's something more urgent first.
Ceto didn't expect you to bring back a medkit.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Don't bother. It's a scratch. I wouldn't have noticed if you hadn't— Mmph!
[CG: Wound Treatment Close-up]
The sharp sting of your fingers probing the wound cuts her sentence short.
You don't stop, continuing to gently clean the gashes on her back with a precious reserve of fresh water.
Looks like the wounds from last night reopened. Does it hurt?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: No. I'm used to it.

options: I don't believe you. Should I press a little harder?
That doesn't sound like a healthy thing to get used to.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hey!

A brief, weary smile passes between you. The sea breeze carries the humid, metallic scent of blood and sweat. You see her muscles tense, a visible battle against her instinctive reaction to the smell.
In response, your own movements slow, your touch gentling. At this proximity, the sound of your breathing intertwines. This time, she doesn't pull away.
As you tend to her wounds, you finally see the map of old injuries covering her body—some faded to scars, others freshly scabbed, and a few still openly weeping.
Has anyone ever told you you have no sense of humor?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Has anyone ever told you you have a death wish?
Actually, yeah. Plenty. But from someone who was sending out signals, saying she was gonna die fighting monsters? You don't get to lecture me about having a death wish.
[CG: Ceto's Profile During Treatment]

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Quit nagging already.

You fall silent, your world narrowing to the task of stemming the bleeding and securing the bandages. The only sounds bridging the quiet between you are the crackle of the fire and the relentless crash of waves. It is a small surprise, then, when she is the one who finally speaks.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Miles... he was always the social one. Always dragging everyone together to try his latest "masterpiece." He was probably just lonely down there. Saw you and thought, "Finally, some company."
I know. When I first saw him underwater... he was still smiling.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Same as when I found him back then. His mind was gone, but he was still smiling, mumbling something. Guess what he said.

options: I'm the greatest lighthouse keeper alive!
This pathetic Black Tide can't take me down!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Heh... close enough. He said:

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Blood outlasts electricity.
[CG: Chief's Profile During Treatment]

The sky bleeds into a deep orange-red as the sun sinks beneath the horizon. In the distance, waves crash against the reef in a rhythmic pulse, as if the Crippled Dawg itself is murmuring its assent to the prophecy: Blood outlasts electricity.
If I were Miles, I definitely didn't bring that ship back because I "had a death wish." And I don't think Herbert was trying to end his life when he went for the Hypercubes, either.
They wanted to live more than anyone. They wanted everyone to live.
Blood continues to seep out, and you cover it with layer after layer of cloth.

Maybe you're right. We are alike. Even when I was surrounded by those things under the sea, I never stopped wanting to see the sun the next morning. No rescue, no supplies... didn't matter. I was going to find a way.
Far away, someone is still waiting for me. Someone who needs me.
[CG: Duo Wound Treatment]

You tell her about your first, contentious encounter with Syndicate's "little rat" after taking office, and how you watched her grow from a girl without a sense of self into someone who learned to feel, to care.
You describe the DisCity you know—a place slowly stirring back to life, yet with undercurrents still swirling beneath its fragile peace.
Ceto is as silent as ever, but you sense a rare, focused attention. This world beyond the Black Tide is a foreign concept to her, a place that only existed in the campfire stories of fallen comrades.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: DisCity...
Pensively, she repeats the name she's heard countless times in those brief respites from battle. It still sounds foreign on her tongue.
It seems she has no stories of her own to offer in return. Her eyes follow your hands as you tie the bandage into an ugly, clumsy bow. Finally, she speaks:

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The meat's ready. Eat.
[Sunset Background]
Over the fire, the monster's leg sizzles and pops, releasing a surprisingly savory aroma, a far cry from the foul stench you anticipated. After two days without food, it smells almost appetizing.

The first bite reveals a firm texture, followed by an unexpected yet delicious flavor—a mild, innate spiciness and a savory saltiness. For a moment, the taste is so rich and unusual that it almost makes you forget the origin of the meat.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Miles spent forever figuring this out. Used me and Sienna as his lab rats until he got the contamination low enough. It's not completely safe; eat too much, you'll get sick. But it'll keep you alive.
She simply watches you eat, making no move to take any for herself. Despite her obvious hunger, she is restraining her instincts, just as she earlier resisted having her wounds treated.
Why aren't you eating? Did you poison it?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Don't flatter yourself. If this island had anything as useful as poison, I wouldn't waste it on you.
She turns her face away, the usual disdain in her tone. But before she turns back, a piece of steaming meat is already there, blocking her path. You have anticipated her movement perfectly.
Well, if it's a lighthouse keeper's specialty, we shouldn't let it go to waste.
Her hand rises to push it away, then freezes mid-motion.

The dog tags on your wrist have caught the dying light, polished by you to a brilliant shine, their engravings sharp and clear as if newly minted. She recognizes them instantly, exactly as you intended.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: When did you—
I found them in the toolbox. I thought Miles might have had one on him too, so I looked a little longer underwater. Sorry for making you come get me.
You place the tags in her hand. She stares at the copper plates in her palm, gleaming like new yet etched with names from a forgotten era.
Around her, the savory aroma of roasted meat hangs in the air. She has mastered the recipe perfectly; it's a scent more familiar to her than any other.
[Ceto's Flashback]

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Sienna! That can was for Ceto! She's a growing girl. Who said you could open it?

steps.speaker: Sienna
steps.content: Hehe, don't be so stingy. Mackerel is the best with a drink. Brings out the flavor. Ceto's too young to appreciate it anyway.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: You opened the booze, too? That was our emergency disinfectant! I swear...

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: Relax! Eat up! The days of pinching pennies are over. I've mastered cooking monster legs. It's a hundred times better than this canned stuff!

steps.speaker: Sienna
steps.content: Well... maybe our little Ceto should be the taste-tester...

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: You turning your nose up at my cooking? I'll have you know Captain Fynn herself appointed me chef of Lighthouse Seven! You know what, I'll go back out tomorrow and find you some canned beef and potatoes then.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: You know, you're right. <color=#fb9259>Tomorrow</color> could bring anything. How about pouring me a bit of that?

steps.speaker: Sienna
steps.content: Sure thing... Hey, wait. Where's my can? Ceto—?! You little sneak, when did you... Get back here! No fair hogging it all!
[End of Flashback]
I saw the inscriptions on the lighthouse's base. The past of the lighthouse keepers... A story DisCity doesn't even know anymore.
But you still know. You remember why they came, the duty they upheld. You're their living legacy.
Ceto takes the meat. At first, her bites are tentative, but restraint quickly shatters. She eats faster, more ravenously, devouring it with a primal urgency.

The smoked aroma floods her senses. Her teeth tear through tough muscle fibers, her throat working relentlessly to swallow the rich, warm protein. Heat courses down her esophagus, flooding into her limbs. This is the flesh of a monster, nurtured by the Black Tide—a creature that fed on the blood and bones of countless lighthouse keepers.

Bite after bite, sensation ignites along her nerves. Her heartbeat drums in her ears, her breathing grows sharp and clear. Beneath the bandages, she feels her flesh knitting itself back together in a frenzy of itching, burning regeneration. And finally, she reclaims a warmth lost to time—
This is what it means to be <color=#fb9259>alive</color>.
[Beach, Night]

From the shore, you watch Ceto. At the base of the lighthouse, she paces off steps with a strange, ritual precision, finally marking a spot on the ground. Then, the long, solitary work of digging begins.
Need a hand?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Almost done. Here, help me with this. Don't drop it.
You step forward to help her lift a tightly wrapped bundle from the earth. It is heavy and cumbersome, standing nearly half a person's height.
What is it?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The last piece you need to repair the lighthouse.
She opens the waterproof tarp, then carefully, almost reverently, peels back the inner layers.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: A spare lens for the beacon light.
[Ceto's Flashback]
Four Hours After the Black Tide Contamination Outbreak

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Have I told you about Sienna? Of all the survivors... she's the one I hated most.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: She served under Fynn. After the contamination wiped out her unit, she was the only one left. So she gathered up all their gear... and came to find Fynn.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Someone's there?!

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: It's the radio operator from Lighthouse Two. What's she doing out here alone?
Ceto quickly adjusted her telescope, bringing the figure in the boat into focus. It was a young woman in a lighthouse keeper's uniform, waving her arms in the precise gestures of semaphore.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: What is she saying?

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: She says... Lighthouse Two is gone. Contamination wiped it out. She's bringing critical supplies to regroup with us.
The girl in the lifeboat pointed to a lens wrapped in bloodstained cloth beside her, using semaphore to signal the message:
<size=50><color=#fb9259>"The Last Light"</color></size>
